title: The Guy Who Built It From a Garage

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "The storefront actually took off. The local paper wants to run a piece — 'the guy who built it out of a garage.'"

options.text: Does the piece mention your partner at all?
You earned every bit of that on your own.
Reporters never get anything right anyway.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "...Not really. I didn't correct them when they asked."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You turn over the top card.

options.text: This card's warmth is real, but it warns against centering the whole story on yourself.
Then you should turn the interview down entirely.
This card doesn't have anything to do with credit.

elaboration: Even the Sun can burn — the warning here isn't against enjoying success, it's against letting confidence tip into making the whole story about you.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "So the Sun's telling me not to enjoy this?"

options.text: No — enjoy it fully, that part's earned. Just make sure the truth in the story includes both of you.
Correct — you should feel guilty about it.
The Sun says none of this actually matters.

elaboration: This is pure, uncomplicated joy, genuinely earned — the card just asks that the truth of the story stays bigger than your part alone in it.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "...Yeah. I'll call the reporter back, get the story right."
